title: HDRTransDC High Dynamic Range Image Reconstruction with Transformer Deformation Convolution

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper repeatedly claims the DWFB 'spatially and adaptively selects useful information across frames' (Abstract, Sec. 3, contributions), yet immediately after generating the dynamic weight it states: 'we use the weight Δw that is shared in spatial dimension and fully connected in channel dimension'. A weight shared across the spatial dimension is by definition not spatially adaptive; this directly contradicts the stated motivation (that convolutions 'share fusion weights across the entire feature' and therefore cannot 'spatially and dynamically highlight the information of an appropriate image').

Q is generated from the reference tokens Z_ref while K and V are generated from the non-reference tokens Z_non (Eq. 2), which makes the operation a cross-attention; nevertheless Eq. (3) and the surrounding text describe it as 'multi-headed self-attention (MSA)'. Furthermore, the residual in Eq. (3) adds Z_non to an attention output whose queries come from Z_ref, which is inconsistent with the stated goal of producing offsets that describe the ref-to-non-ref correspondence and is never justified.

The text argues 'Because the final offsets represent the position difference between the extracted features and the generated feature, we add the learnable absolute positional encoding Pos on the non-reference features F_non'. If the offsets encode a positional *difference* between reference and non-reference locations, positional information must be available in both the query (reference) and key (non-reference) branches; adding positional encoding only to the non-reference features is inconsistent with the stated rationale.

The deformable-convolution formulation F^a_non(p) = Σ_k m_k · F_non(p + p_k + ΔP(p,k)) omits the learned modulation/mask term of (modulated) deformable convolution and treats m_k only as a fixed kernel weight; as written the equation is a plain convolution with learned sampling offsets, so the claimed ability to 'compensate for occluded content' by weighting the sampled long-range content is not expressed by the stated equation.
